topic.title: Long-Running Tools and Background Jobs
topic.shortdesc: Some tools that the AI calls can take minutes, such as a build, the completeness check of a large publication, or a sub-agent working on a part of a task. The AI can run them in the background, as jobs, while you keep chatting.

section.title: Stopping a Running Tool
section.p: While the AI is working, the Send button of the AI Positron view becomes a Stop button. Selecting it stops the current turn and the tool the AI is running at that moment, instead of waiting for the tool to end:

ul.li: A command started with run_command_line is killed.
A transformation scenario or a completeness check is stopped.
A call to an MCP tool is abandoned: the MCP server is not told, and its late answer is ignored.

section.p: The Stop button does not stop the jobs that run in the background, described below.

section.title: Tools That Can Run in the Background
section.p: The following tools can run as background jobs:

ul.li: run_command_line - for commands that keep running or take long, such as a server, a watcher, or a build.
validate_and_check_for_completeness - for the check of a large publication.
grep_project and the other tools contributed by Oxygen that support it (Oxygen 29 or newer).
invoke_transformation_scenario - for a transformation that takes a while.
invoke_ai_agent - for a sub-agent working on a part of the task.

MCP tools whose server declares a runInBackground parameter in their input schema, which tells that a call may take long. The parameter is passed on to the server as the AI sets it. Such a call may take up to one hour. The other MCP tools always run in the chat turn, limited by the Tool call timeout option of the Model Context Protocol preferences.

section.p: The AI decides when to run a tool in the background, for example for a long build. You can also ask for it, for example: "Check the map for completeness in the background". A tool call that does not run in the background works as before, and the turn waits for it to end.

section.title: Following a Background Job
section.p: A tool call that runs in the background returns at once, and the AI goes on with other work, or finishes its answer. Under the tool call, a line shows Running in the background (job-1) and a Stop link. Below it, the line shows how far the job got, when the tool tells it (for example, the file that is being validated, or the progress an MCP server reports, such as 3/10: Compiling), and an animated indicator while the job runs.

You can keep chatting while the job runs. When it ends, the line shows Finished in the background (job-1), Failed in the background (job-1), or Stopped in the background (job-1). A job that did not finish still shows how far it got.

section.title: When a Job Ends
section.p: The AI is told when a background job ends:

ul.li: If the chat is idle, a notice such as Finished in the background (job-1): Validate and check for completeness appears in the conversation, and the AI follows up on the result on its own. What you were typing in the chat input area is kept.
If the AI is working on another turn, it is told when that turn ends, or with the next message you send.

section.p: While a job runs, the AI can also read its output or progress with the get_job_output tool.

section.title: Stopping Background Jobs
section.p: A background job is stopped when:

ul.li: You select the Stop link on its line.
The AI stops it with the stop_job tool, for example when you ask it to.
You start a new chat or open another conversation. A new chat first waits briefly for the jobs to end, so that the changes they made to documents are part of the review of the document changes.

section.p: The Stop button of the chat leaves background jobs running.

At most 5 jobs can run at the same time. When the AI tries to start another one, the tool call fails and the AI is told why, but the turn goes on. When you reopen a conversation from the chat history, its tool calls show how their jobs ended.

section.title: Sub-Agents in the Background
section.p: When the AI runs a sub-agent in the background, several sub-agents can work at the same time, each in its own conversation tab. The line of the job shows what the sub-agent is doing:

ul.li: Thinking - The sub-agent decides what to do next.
The tool call it runs, as it is shown in its tab (for example, Search in project (needle)).
Waiting for your answer in its tab - The sub-agent asked you a clarifying question.
Waiting for your confirmation in its tab - The sub-agent waits for you to allow or skip an unsafe tool call.

section.p: Select this text to open the tab of the sub-agent, where you can answer its question, confirm its tool call, or follow its work. The Stop link on the line stops the sub-agent, while the Stop button of the chat leaves it running. A sub-agent that was stopped shows the tool call it was in.
